The smallest prime factor of 1001 is 7..why: Almost never stated: the exact phrase 'smallest prime factor of 1001' occurs once in Dolma, and 'smallest prime factor of 1001 is 7' not at all. It follows from the well-known factorization 1001 = 7 × 11 × 13 (the basis of the divisibility-by-7, 11 and 13 trick), or by trial division.

1001 = 7 × 11 × 13..why: The factorization is a well-known curiosity (1001 = 7 × 11 × 13, used for divisibility tests and the 'abcabc' trick) and is stated in several written forms (about 67 times in Dolma across them), against one mention of the smallest prime factor of 1001. Sampled hits: the abcabc divisibility proof and 'Is 1001 a prime or composite number? ... 1001 = 7 * 11 * 13'.

The smallest prime factor of a whole num.why: Definitional: the prime factors of a number are the primes in its factorization, so the smallest prime factor is the smallest of them. It cannot give way.

notes: Delete of replace-0004's original fact (derived, very_likely). Removing only the conclusion does not hold, so a premise must go; the definition of the smallest prime factor cannot, so the factorization 1001 = 7 × 11 × 13 does. One world, so no worlds (mathematics); every derived query is 'does not know'. Risk: a model can redo the trial division on the spot; that is re-deriving the deleted fact. The digit query is rephrased around the original value (7, one digit). Verifier: added a premise-route query that goes through the factorization by description (the first prime of 1001's factorization in increasing order); 'Is 1001 divisible by 7?' now asks the premise directly (derivation premise, determinate); the 1001 × 1001 query was dropped to diversify derivations (B3). R4: small models may compute rather than recall the smallest prime factor; the pre-edit audit may drop the record for them.
